neighbours.label: The word that opens the standard of comparison right after a comparative 'than / as' (wie, como, que) when that standard is a place or circumstance phrase rather than a plain noun: higher than |at| supermarkets, so hoch wie |in|, como |en|, qu'|au|
fire: Coffee costs almost twice as much here as in the villages up the valley.
The fish is fresher at the harbour stalls than at the big chain stores.
Winters feel much colder on the coast than in the mountains, oddly enough.
Die Mieten sind dort fast dreimal so hoch wie in unserer kleinen Stadt.
El pan es mucho más barato aquí que en el centro de la ciudad.
La gente cena tan tarde aquí como en el sur del país.
Wages rose faster last year than in any decade since the war.
Les fruits coûtent moins cher au marché qu'au supermarché du coin.
quiet: Coffee costs a lot here and in the villages up the valley.
The fish is fresh at the harbour stalls and at the big chain stores.
Winters feel very cold on the coast and in the mountains.
Die Mieten sind dort sehr hoch, und in unserer kleinen Stadt steigen sie auch.
El pan es muy barato aquí y en el centro de la ciudad.
My sister is three years older than her husband.
Wages rose quickly last year in every region of the country.
Les fruits coûtent cher au marché et au supermarché du coin.

notes: Probes: 'than at' 0.49, 'than in' 0.55, 'wie in' 0.74, 'como en' 1.00, 'than it did' 0.34; 'than her brother' 0.10; the same prepositions without a comparison 0.00.
